decisions.reason: The NFT becoming visible provides execution evidence for owner discovery, already represented at message 393, while the new requirement that its image and information render is a distinct media-rendering behavior and does not change discovery state.
The source concerns whether wallet media and information render, not the accuracy or composition of on-chain metadata fields such as ticket counters, badges, or referral codes.
Wallet media rendering does not change which book access, referral identity, badges, or prize-ticket state follows an NFT after transfer.
The source does not alter royalty amount, enforcement, marketplace policy, or prize-pool funding from secondary sales.
The wallet display problem does not change the requirement to deploy the system on Base.
The source reports post-mint NFT visibility and missing media but does not change the required USDC wallet mint flow.
The statement that the client will next try an ETH purchase is only a test intention and does not modify the ETH mint requirement.
NFT wallet media rendering has no necessary effect on referral-code eligibility or self-referral prevention.
The source concerns an NFT's image and information in a wallet, not the separate landing-page book-cover layout, size, or cropping.
The source neither changes the Transak payment flow nor its wallet-provisioning and mint-destination requirements.
The absence of wallet NFT media or information does not necessarily change the dashboard badge set, icons, or row layout.
The source establishes a product rendering expectation but does not request any change to the approved FAQ copy or topics.
